title: The Diplomat Who Defied His Government to Save 6,000 Jews #shorts
description:
He defied his own government — and saved six thousand lives with a pen.

Chiune Sugihara was Japan's vice-consul in Kaunas, Lithuania, in the summer of 1940. As Jewish refugees crowded the consulate begging for transit visas to escape the Nazis, he asked Tokyo for permission three times. Three times, the answer was no.

So he disobeyed. For twenty-nine days, he wrote more than two thousand visas by hand — eighteen hours a day — sending around six thousand people east across the Soviet Union to freedom. Even as his train pulled away, he kept signing visas through the window.

After the war, Japan cast him aside. He lived in obscurity for decades, never knowing how many he saved — until a survivor found him in 1968, holding one of those visas.
